key_insight: A neural-network policy optimized by a genetic algorithm can learn minimum-time navigation in 2D flows, matching optimal-control solutions and handling turbulent environments.
engineering_relevance: This offers a compact, parallelizable route-planning method for autonomous vessels or microrobots moving through complex flows when fast, robust trajectory computation is needed.
method: Parameterize the navigation rule with a neural network.
Evolve policy parameters with a genetic algorithm using selection and mutation, without crossover.
Evaluate in benchmark flows and turbulent cases against optimal-control, Q-learning, and actor-critic baselines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the learned policy recovers analytical/numerical optima in benchmark problems and outperforms Q-learning and one-step actor-critic, while remaining robust to starting-point variation and small unresolved turbulence.
watch_item: Robustness depends on unresolved fluctuations staying small relative to the vessel slip velocity, so performance may degrade in stronger or less-resolved turbulence.
paper_title: Learning minimum-time navigation policies in two-dimensional flows with a genetic algorithm
